A.title: FED-3/FED-4 canonical per-author statement streams with gap buffering, fork detection and tombstones
A.goal: Implement in packages/federation a persistent, kernel-backed admission layer for CTR-FED-001 FED-3 and FED-4 on top of the existing verifyEnvelope primitive: per-author (did:key) contiguous seq/prev chains; contiguous statements are accepted and become the author head; out-of-order statements are buffered as gaps (bounded per author and globally) for at most 24 h, resolved in order when their predecessor arrives, and expired with a typed reason afterwards; duplicates (same cid) are idempotent; a second distinct cid at an already accepted (author, seq), or a statement whose prev does not equal the accepted cid at seq-1, is a FORK: the author stream freezes with both envelopes retained as evidence and nothing is overwritten (no last-writer-wins); stale replays are rejected; everything survives storage close/reopen (replay from persisted records); FED-4 tombstones classrup.federation.tombstone/v1 {target: cid|id, reason} are accepted only from the target's author (origin-relay signing deferred with an explicit limit), schedule purge of the target content within 24 h, and are retained 180 days; unauthorized tombstones are rejected. Provide an explicit integration seam so the existing alpha per-subject publication chains (classrup.alpha.*) keep working untouched and can later be routed through this layer. Deliver the exact fixtures PR #15 asked for: same-author/different-subject gap and fork handling, positive sequential and duplicate admission, bounded 24h expiry, and storage-reopen replay.
A.constraints: Only packages/federation/src/** (new files plus index.ts exports) and tests/integration/federation-*.test.ts. Isomorphic TypeScript (no node: imports). Persist with kernel repos/transactions (defineRepo, writeRepo, Tx) in the caller's tenant; injected clock (now: number) everywhere; every buffer and evidence set bounded with documented limits; typed error codes defined in F11 module.spec.yaml files (reuse existing codes such as FED_SIGNATURE_INVALID; append new codes to the owning module spec only if missing, keeping pnpm spec:check at 0 errors and not adding warnings); never modify classrup.alpha.* semantics or vault/identity/mutiny/kernel code; verifyEnvelope remains the only signature authority; test titles carry TEST-PS-NNN-09.Tnn IDs from the owning specs.
lenses: protocol correctness and formal ordering guarantees (think like a distributed-systems engineer: define the exact state machine per author stream, prove no silent overwrite, enumerate every ordering interleaving)
adversarial security (think like an attacker: replay, fork injection, buffer exhaustion, clock games, tombstone forgery, cross-author confusion, storage tampering between sessions)

minimal faithful implementation on the existing kernel (think like the engineer who will write it this week: smallest set of repos/records, simplest APIs, reuse of tx.records/leases/migrations, exact test files)

B.title: Private-record encryption at rest for the browser vault with forward migration and tamper handling
B.goal: Encrypt every vault table stored in IndexedDB (records, outbox, inbox, idempotency, leases, deadLetters, sync, blobs, migrations) so that nothing but a plaintext bootstrap blob in the meta table is readable without the passphrase. Design: a per-vault random 32-byte data-encryption key (DEK) wrapping with a key-encryption key derived from the passphrase; at most ONE scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) derivation per unlock after migration (the identity signing key and the DEK must both unwrap from that single derivation) while remaining able to read existing vaults created by the alpha (ProtectedIdentity in a plaintext record) and existing classrup.vault.alpha_backup/v1 bundles; per-row XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a fresh 24-byte nonce and associated data that binds table, key, vault/key identifier and format version so rows cannot be swapped between tables, keys or vaults; forward migration of an existing plaintext vault on the first successful unlock (atomic or resumable with a persisted marker; fail closed on interruption, never leave a half-plaintext vault that is accepted later; never silently downgrade); after migration plaintext rows are rejected as corruption; wrong passphrase fails without touching data; a flipped ciphertext byte or a row with mismatching associated data makes open fail closed with a typed error (no partial data); lock() zeroes key material; exportBackup/restoreBackup keep working; isInitialized reads only the bootstrap blob; optional passphrase change by rewrapping the DEK without re-encrypting rows if it fits cleanly. Document exactly what rollback of individual rows to older ciphertext does or does not detect and why.
B.constraints: Modify only packages/kernel/src/storage/indexeddb.ts, new packages/kernel/src/storage/at-rest*.ts (or a similarly named new file), packages/vault/src/vault.ts (create/unlock/migration flow), new key-material helper files under packages/identity/src/ (do not change identity.ts semantics), and tests (packages/kernel/src/storage/*.test.ts for new files, packages/vault/src/vault.test.ts adaptations, tests/integration/vault-encryption*.test.ts). Do not touch memory-driver.ts, sqlite.ts, outbox/*, observability/*, federation, mutiny. Isomorphic (WebCrypto plus the already pinned @noble/hashes 2.4.0 and @noble/ciphers 2.4.0 MIT; no new dependencies). Keep the openVault/vaultFromStorage public API backward compatible for callers (apps/pwa/src/main.ts must not need changes beyond what the design states explicitly and justifies). Keep all existing tests passing (fake-indexeddb). Bound memory: the snapshot model decrypts all rows at open; state the cost and limits. Key material zeroed on lock; no key material in errors or logs; typed errors (DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE with a reason, or a new code defined in the owning spec).
lenses: applied cryptography engineering (key hierarchy, nonce/AAD discipline, KDF reuse, downgrade and rollback resistance, memory hygiene; cite the exact primitives and formats)

adversarial security and data-loss prevention (attacker with a copy of the IndexedDB files or a tampering browser extension, interrupted migration, concurrent tabs, wrong passphrase, storage quota failure mid-migration: what must never happen)

minimal faithful implementation on the existing IndexedDB adapter and vault composition (exact insertion points in indexeddb.ts persist/loadSnapshot, the meta table, VAULT_DB_VERSION bump, how vault.ts sequences open→bootstrap→unlock→decrypt, fake-indexeddb test plan)

C.title: ADR-0013 account/device model: device linking, key rotation, revocation and one-time recovery kit
C.goal: Implement in packages/identity a local-first account/device model: an account is identified by a stable accountId (the did:key of the genesis key; the existing single alpha identity becomes the genesis device with no migration), plus an append-only signed identity log of statements (type classrup.identity.event/v1 or a small family of versioned types) chained per account with seq/prev, each signed by a key that is authorized at that point of the log: device_link (new device DID with a counter-signature proving possession of the new key), device_revoke (cannot leave the account without an active device unless the account is explicitly closed), key_rotate (link new then revoke old, atomic in one statement or a defined pair), recovery_setup (registers the DID of an account recovery key whose private key is encrypted by a one-time recovery kit secret: generated once from 256 random bits, shown once, never re-displayable, encoded in a form humans can transcribe without a new dependency), recovery_claim (signed by the recovery key: links a new device and revokes all previous devices, effective after a dispute window of 72 h during which any still-active device may sign recovery_dispute which freezes the account for explicit manual resolution). Receivers fold a verified log deterministically into a portable identity document {accountId, devices[{did,label,status,since}], recoveryDid, state active|frozen|closed, head} ; out-of-order events are held until their predecessor arrives (bounded, expiring); any fork (two distinct events at one seq, or prev mismatch) freezes the document with retained evidence and no silent acceptance; replayed/duplicate events are idempotent; events signed by a revoked or unknown key are rejected; provide isAuthorizedSigner(document, did, atIso) and accountOf(did) resolution for federation receivers; persist the log and document in the vault with kernel repos; keep recovery key material P4 (sealed with the existing seal/unseal at rest, only ever unsealed with the kit secret).
C.constraints: New files under packages/identity/src/ plus exports in packages/identity/src/index.ts and tests (packages/identity/src/*.test.ts, tests/integration/identity-*.test.ts). Do not modify identity.ts logic (reuse createIdentity/unlockIdentity/seal/unseal as they are), vault.ts, federation internals (use signEnvelope/verifyEnvelope as the only signing/verification path), kernel or mutiny. Isomorphic; no new dependencies (if a word list is needed, justify an embedded one explicitly or choose an encoding that needs none). Injected clock. Bounded log sizes and hold buffers with documented limits. Typed error codes from the owning module.spec.yaml (07_Identity accounts/recovery and 16_Security cryptography); append new codes only where missing, keeping pnpm spec:check at 0 errors with no new warnings. Test titles carry TEST-PS-NNN-09.Tnn IDs. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: relays are out of scope; state that honestly.
lenses: identity protocol design (think like someone designing a key-transparency/sequencer-free device log: exact event schemas, authorization rules at each point in the log, fold semantics, what freezes vs rejects, how rotation and recovery interact with federation authorship)

adversarial security (stolen device, stolen but not-yet-revoked key racing a revocation, forged recovery claim, replay of old link events, log forks from two offline devices, kit brute force, kit reuse, social-engineering of the dispute window)

minimal faithful implementation on the existing identity and federation primitives (exact TypeScript files, reuse of signEnvelope/verifyEnvelope and seal/unseal, kernel repos for persistence, concrete fast-check properties and integration tests)

D.title: CTR-IOX-001 IOX-2 read-only import preflight (dry run) and idempotent import into an existing vault
D.goal: Implement packages/vault/src/import.ts: preflightBackup(unlocked, bundle, passphrase) is strictly read-only and returns a complete report: format and version, bundle author and whether it matches the unlocked principal, per-type counts, records classified as new / identical / conflicting (with local and bundle revisions and ids), unsupported record types, excluded scopes (media blobs, outbox/inbox, leases, delivery state) with an explicit disclosure, validator failures, and overall verdict; importBackup(unlocked, bundle, passphrase, options) applies the same classification inside ONE kernel transaction after all parsing, codec restoreData normalization and async validators have run, so a corrupted or conflicting later record leaves nothing written; repeat import of an identical bundle is idempotent (zero writes, reported as such); identical records are skipped; conflicting records (same type and id, different revision or data) reject the whole import by default with the conflict list, or are skipped under an explicit options.onConflict: 'skip' mode which never overwrites; a bundle authored by a different principal is rejected before any decryption of records is retained (never import another user's private data into this vault); restored coordination records keep the existing freeze-for-review semantics; a migration registry handles previous-major bundle formats (today only classrup.vault.alpha_backup/v1; define the hook and its tests); the existing restoreBackup fail-closed empty-vault path is unchanged; all sizes bounded as in vault.ts.
D.constraints: New packages/vault/src/import.ts and its test file, minimal export wiring in packages/vault/src/index.ts; use only the UnlockedVault public surface (principal, identity, storage) plus the BackupCodec list and the existing seal/unseal and verifyEnvelope; do not modify vault.ts unlock/create/restore logic (the merge step will add one method to UnlockedVault if the design asks for it; specify that exact diff). Isomorphic, no new dependencies, injected clock where time matters. Typed errors from CTR-ERR-001 or the owning specs (F10.S01.M03 export, F15.S03.M02 backups). Test titles carry TEST-PS-NNN-09.Tnn IDs; tests use fake-indexeddb or the memory storage seam exactly as vault.test.ts does.
lenses: data-integrity engineering (classification semantics, atomicity, idempotency proofs, exact report schema, migration registry design)

adversarial security and privacy (malicious bundle: forged author, mixed-principal records, oversized, duplicate ids with different payloads, validator bypass, crafted conflicts to cause partial writes, replay of an old bundle to resurrect deleted records; what the design guarantees and what it cannot)

minimal faithful implementation on the existing vault code (reuse the restoreBackup parsing pipeline without duplicating it, exact function signatures, how tests construct bundles with exportBackup and mutate them)

E.title: Value balancing (tolerance, compensation legs, pinned FX quotes) and quantity-aware wants and holds for barter cycles
E.goal: Implement in packages/mutiny (new value_balancing/ module plus minimal, additive changes in cycle_matching and trade_proposals) and packages/bazaar (additive quantity support): CTR-MNY-001 money arithmetic (bigint minor units from decimal strings, HALF_EVEN rounding once at the end, FX quote {id, base, quote, rate:{num,den}, source, asOf, expiresAt} conversion exactly as MNY-4, a minimal currency registry with ISO 4217 minor units for a documented subset plus BTC 8, ETH 18, USDC 6, unknown currency rejected); MNY-5 tolerance (default 5 % of the larger side or a configured absolute minimum, per-participant overrides) applied per participant to the value given vs received in a cycle; explicit compensation legs computed deterministically with integer math (payer, payee, Money, pinned quote id when cross-currency) that bring every participant within tolerance with the minimum number of legs for the deterministic algorithm chosen, as claims to be settled externally with no custody; cross-currency cycles require quotes pinned ≤ 24 h (N16) and a cycle deadline no later than the earliest quote expiry, otherwise re-quote with fresh consent; quantity-aware inventory: listings carry quantity (default 1, existing data unchanged), wants carry requested quantity, holds reserve k units, available = quantity minus active holds, admission edges and cycle legs carry quantities, feasibility recheck counts units, no over-commitment under concurrent proposals (property test). Proposal digest compatibility: existing classrup.alpha.proposal_revision/v1 snapshots without compensation or quantities must produce byte-identical digests and remain accepted; new terms are introduced through a versioned extension the design specifies (new statement version or an explicitly versioned optional section) with tests proving old fixtures are unchanged. All of this stays within the existing bounds of the matching engine.
E.constraints: Only packages/mutiny/src/** (new value_balancing/ files; additive edits to cycle_matching and trade_proposals), packages/bazaar/src/listings/** (additive), their test files, tests/integration/mutiny-value*.test.ts, and append-only test rows in the owning module.spec.yaml files (F02.S04.M01/M02/M03, F02.S02.M05, F02.S03.M02, F01.S03.M01, F09.S03.M01/M02/M03) keeping pnpm spec:check at 0 errors with no new warnings. Never floats; bigint only. Deterministic given inputs and injected clock. Existing tests (packages/mutiny/src/**, tests/integration/mutiny-*.test.ts, tests/integration/alpha-security.test.ts) must pass unchanged. Keep every statement type versioned; never change the meaning of existing classrup.alpha.* payloads. No custody, no settlement claims: compensation legs are obligations evidenced by signatures only. Test titles carry TEST-PS-NNN-09.Tnn IDs; use fast-check for properties.
lenses: algorithm and numerical design (exact integer formulas, rounding placement, compensation-leg algorithm with proof of termination and minimality for the chosen strategy, quantity feasibility as a flow/counting problem, complexity bounds)

adversarial economics and security (valuation lies, stale or expired quotes, rounding attacks, tolerance gaming, over-commitment races across concurrent proposals, replayed holds, participants exploiting compensation legs; what freezes vs rejects)

minimal faithful implementation on the existing admission -> matching -> proposal -> coordination pipeline (exact types to extend, digest compatibility strategy with fixtures, kernel callbacks for quantity holds, test files)
